title: Pregnancy Recipes: Iron-and-Folate Bowls You Can Cook in 30 Minutes
excerpt: Three tasty recipes pairing heme/non-heme iron with vitamin C — Vietnamese-inspired bowls with clear portions and food-safety notes.
content:
## Introduction
During pregnancy, it's essential to provide the body with sufficient iron and folate. Iron helps create red blood cells, while folate supports the development of the fetus. However, choosing iron-rich and folate-rich foods can be a challenge. Here are three simple and delicious recipes that combine iron with vitamin C, helping pregnant women have a nutritious meal.

## Recipe 1: Grilled Chicken and Spinach Bowl
* 1 cup brown rice
* 1 grilled chicken breast (30g)
* 1 cup steamed spinach
* 1 orange (vitamin C)
* 1 tablespoon olive oil
* Salt and pepper

Grill the chicken with olive oil and seasonings, then serve with brown rice and steamed spinach. Eat with an orange to enhance iron absorption.

## Recipe 2: Baked Salmon and Broccoli Bowl
* 1 cup brown rice
* 1 baked salmon fillet (30g)
* 1 cup steamed broccoli
* 1 bell pepper (vitamin C)
* 1 tablespoon olive oil
* Salt and pepper

Bake the salmon with olive oil and seasonings, then serve with brown rice and steamed broccoli. Eat with a bell pepper to enhance iron absorption.

## Recipe 3: Beef and Kale Stir-Fry Bowl
* 1 cup brown rice
* 1 beef stir-fry (30g)
* 1 cup steamed kale
* 1 lemon (vitamin C)
* 1 tablespoon olive oil
* Salt and pepper

Stir-fry the beef with olive oil and seasonings, then serve with brown rice and steamed kale. Eat with a lemon to enhance iron absorption.

## Food Safety Notes
When pregnant, it's crucial to pay attention to food safety to avoid bacterial infections and other health issues. Ensure that all foods are cooked thoroughly and stored properly.

## Conclusion
The three recipes above provide a rich source of iron and folate, helping pregnant women have a nutritious meal. Remember to combine iron with vitamin C to enhance iron absorption. And don't forget to follow food safety guidelines to ensure the health of both mother and baby.

Please consult your healthcare provider before making any changes to your diet. They can provide personalized advice and guidance to ensure you're getting the necessary nutrients for a healthy pregnancy.
